text:
NextItNet’s foundation is stacked residual, dilated causal convolutions: larger receptive fields capture longer dependencies while preserving autoregressive prediction. Searches found related multiscale and gating research, but no verified 2023–2026 paper establishing the exact proposed gated adaptive-receptive-field NextItNet extension. [Original NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf). Related evidence: ScaleRec (2025 DOI; January 2026 issue) combines multiple temporal scales, locality biases, context-adaptive preference aggregation and masking of redundant interactions; its Transformer backbone provides motivation rather than a family-preserving implementation. [ScaleRec](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596).

The closest recency mechanism found is MARS, a June 2026 preprint: real timestamps generate summaries at multiple decay rates, combined through a context-adaptive gate. Its reported gains concern Transformer/Mamba implementations, so transfer to NextItNet remains untested. [MARS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03718). ICSRec (2023 preprint) supplies complementary intent evidence, learning intent representations through contrastive supervision over subsequences. [ICSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14318).

Research hypothesis: retain NextItNet residual causal blocks, add jointly trained convolution branches with small and large dilations, and learn context-dependent gates over their features. An optional timestamp-decay input could help suppress stale interactions; this is a proposed adaptation, not an established result. Compare fixed versus learned scale weights, gates enabled versus disabled, and positional recency versus timestamp recency under matched capacity and training budgets. Select using four-category macro validation HR@10, with one network/checkpoint per category and final-nonpadding readout for left-padded histories.
